Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Ads setting for sites with intrusive ads
Description: This setting controls whether ads are blocked on sites with intrusive ads. Intrusive ads are typically ads that push invasive, unwelcomed, and irrelevant ads in front of consumers. These ads can pop up unexpectedly, block the host page, open new pages and windows, or play video and audio at inopportune times.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Blocking intrusive ads on sites with poor ad experiences is low-risk and improves security posture. Only deviate if an internal site is incorrectly flagged — add it to the ads exception list rather than disabling globally.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Allow Basic authentication for HTTP
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling Basic auth over plain HTTP prevents credentials being sent in cleartext. No valid reason to enable this in 2025; if an internal app requires it, migrate the app to HTTPS first.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Allow Google Cast to connect to Cast devices on all IP addresses
Description: This policy setting controls whether Google Cast is able to connect to all IP Addresses or only private IP Addresses as defined in RFC1918 (IPv4) and RFC4193 (IPv6).
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling Google Cast removes the ability to cast browser content to Chromecast/Cast-capable devices. Only enable if users legitimately use Chromecast for presentations; low security risk either way.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Allow cross-origin HTTP Authentication prompts
Description: This policy setting controls whether third-party sub-content can open a HTTP Basic Auth dialog and is typically disabled.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Blocking cross-origin HTTP authentication prompts prevents credential phishing via embedded cross-origin resources. Rarely needed in modern SMB web apps; only enable if a specific intranet application requires it.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Allow download restrictions
Description: This policy setting controls whether Microsoft Edge blocks certain types of downloads, and prevents users from bypassing security warnings, depending on the classification of Safe Browsing.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Blocking dangerous downloads reduces malware risk significantly. The configured value (Block malicious downloads) is the recommended CIS balance; only relax if a specific LOB workflow requires downloading file types flagged by Safe Browsing.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Allow import of data from other browsers on each Microsoft Edge launch
Description: This policy setting controls if users will get a prompt following each Microsoft Edge launch to import their data from other browsers. Microsoft Edge will import data such as passwords, bookmarks, cookies, browsing history, and payment information depending on which browser this data is being imported from. At this time, Microsoft Edge can only import data from Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Internet Explorer, and some thirdparty Password Managers.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling auto-import on each launch prevents personal browser data leaking into the managed Edge profile. Users who migrate from another browser may notice this; provide guidance on first-run import only.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Allow importing of autofill form data
Description: This policy setting controls the user's ability to import autofill data from other browsers into Microsoft Edge
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling address autofill prevents the browser from storing personal address data locally. Low operational impact; users can still manually enter addresses. Acceptable trade-off for data privacy.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Allow importing of browser settings
Description: This policy setting controls whether users are able to import settings from another browser into Microsoft Edge
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Blocking import of saved passwords, autofill data, or settings from other browsers prevents unmanaged credential bleed-over. Low operational impact for users who are already on managed Edge profiles.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Allow importing of home page settings
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Blocking import of saved passwords, autofill data, or settings from other browsers prevents unmanaged credential bleed-over. Low operational impact for users who are already on managed Edge profiles.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Allow importing of payment info
Description: This policy setting controls whether users are able to import payment information from another browser into Microsoft Edge as well as whether payment information is imported on first use.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Blocking import of saved passwords, autofill data, or settings from other browsers prevents unmanaged credential bleed-over. Low operational impact for users who are already on managed Edge profiles.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Allow importing of saved passwords
Description: This policy setting controls whether users are able to import saved passwords from another browser into Microsoft Edge as well as whether passwords are imported on first use.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling the built-in password manager forces users to a centrally managed password manager (e.g., 1Password, Bitwarden). Communicate the policy change and ensure an approved alternative is deployed before enforcing.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Allow importing of search engine settings
Description: This policy setting controls whether users are able to import search engine settings from another browser into Microsoft Edge as well as whether said setting is imported on first use.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Blocking import of saved passwords, autofill data, or settings from other browsers prevents unmanaged credential bleed-over. Low operational impact for users who are already on managed Edge profiles.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Allow managed extensions to use the Enterprise Hardware Platform API
Description: This policy setting allows extensions installed by enterprise policies to be allowed to use the Enterprise Hardware Platform API. This API handles requests from extensions for the manufacturer and model of the hardware platform where the browser is running.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Blocking external or unmanaged extensions prevents malicious browser add-ons. Use the Intune app deployment or Edge extension allowlist to deploy approved extensions rather than enabling open install.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Allow queries to a Browser Network Time service
Description: This policy setting controls whether Microsoft Edge can send queries to a network time service for accurate timestamps. This check helps in validation of certificates.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Allowing Edge to query a browser network time service improves certificate validation accuracy. Low-risk to enable; only block if strict egress filtering prevents outbound time service queries.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Allow remote debugging
Description: This policy setting controls whether users may use remote debugging. This feature allows remote debugging of live content on a Windows 10 or later device from a Windows or macOS computer.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Allowing remote debugging creates a significant attack surface — any process can inspect page content and credentials. This should always be disabled in managed SMB endpoints; there is no valid production use case for enabling it.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Allow the audio sandbox to run
Description: This policy setting controls whether audio processes in Microsoft Edge run in a sandbox.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: The audio sandbox isolates the audio process to limit the impact of audio codec exploits. Disabling it should only be considered if a specific audio driver incompatibility is documented.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Allow user feedback
Description: This policy setting controls whether users are able to utilize the Edge Feedback feature to send feedback, suggestions and surveys to Microsoft as well as issue reports.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling built-in feedback and support channels prevents telemetry and user data from being sent to Microsoft/Google via these paths. IT support should provide an alternative channel; users may initially miss the quick feedback button.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Allow websites to query for available payment methods
Description: This policy setting allows you to set whether a website can check to see if the user has payment methods saved.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Preventing websites from querying available payment methods reduces fingerprinting and payment data exposure. Negligible impact for most SMB users; only relevant if a web app relies on the Payment Request API.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Blocks external extensions from being installed
Description: This policy setting determines whether external extensions (an extension that is not installed from the Chrome Web Store) can be installed.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Blocking external or unmanaged extensions prevents malicious browser add-ons. Use the Intune app deployment or Edge extension allowlist to deploy approved extensions rather than enabling open install.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Clear browsing data when Microsoft Edge closes
Description: This policy controls whether web browser data, such as forms, passwords and visited sites is deleted each time Microsoft Edge is closed.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Enforcing browsing data clearing on exit reduces residual data exposure on shared or unattended devices. Users on dedicated personal devices may find this disruptive; balance privacy requirements with usability.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Clear cached images and files when Microsoft Edge closes
Description: This policy controls whether cached images and files are deleted each time Microsoft Edge closes
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Enforcing browsing data clearing on exit reduces residual data exposure on shared or unattended devices. Users on dedicated personal devices may find this disruptive; balance privacy requirements with usability.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Clear history for IE and IE mode every time you exit
Description: This policy setting controls if history will be cleared for Internet Explorer (IE) and IE mode every time a user exits the browser.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Enforcing browsing data clearing on exit reduces residual data exposure on shared or unattended devices. Users on dedicated personal devices may find this disruptive; balance privacy requirements with usability.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Compose is enabled for writing on the web
Description: This policy setting allows the configuration of Compose in Microsoft Edge. Compose provides help for writing with AI-generated text, which lets the user get ideas for writing. This includes elaborating on text, re-writing, changing tone, formatting the text, and more.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling Edge AI writing and image generation features prevents page content from being submitted to Microsoft AI services. Appropriate for environments with data handling obligations; no core productivity feature is lost.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Configure Edge Website Typo Protection
Description: This policy setting configures whether to turn on Edge TyposquattingChecker. The Edge TyposquattingChecker provides warning messages to help protect users from potential typo squatting sites. Typo squatting is a type of social engineering attack which targets internet users who incorrectly type a URL into their web browser rather than using a search engine. Typically, it involves tricking users into visiting malicious websites with URLs that are common misspellings of legitimate websites.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Enabling Edge website typo protection warns users about mistyped URLs that may lead to lookalike phishing sites. Low-friction security feature; only disable if it generates false positives for internal hostnames.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Configure InPrivate mode availability
Description: This policy setting controls whether Edge InPrivate mode is available or even forced for the user.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling InPrivate mode prevents users from circumventing browsing history and web filter policies. Only enable if a specific workflow requires untracked browsing and compensating controls exist.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Configure Microsoft Defender SmartScreen
Description: This policy setting allows configuration of Microsoft Defender SmartScreen. Microsoft Defender SmartScreen helps to identify phishing and malware websites and to make informed decisions about downloads.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Microsoft Defender SmartScreen is a key browser-level phishing and malware protection layer. Only skip if a third-party DNS filter or web proxy already provides equivalent real-time URL reputation checking.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Configure Related Matches in Find on Page
Description: This policy setting specifies how the user receives Related Matches in Find on Page, which provides spellcheck, synonyms, and Q&A results in Microsoft Edge.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling AI-powered 'Related Matches' in Find on Page prevents page content from being sent to Microsoft for fuzzy search. Privacy control; basic Find (Ctrl+F) functionality is unaffected.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Configure the Share experience
Description: This policy setting allows users to be able to access the Share experience from the Settings and More menu in Microsoft Edge, which can allow information to be shared with other apps on the system.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Configuring or disabling the Edge share experience reduces unnecessary data sharing via consumer share targets. Set to ShareAllowed with approved targets only, or disable if no sharing workflow is needed.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Configure the list of names that will bypass the HSTS policy check
Description: This policy setting allows a list of names to be specified that will be exempt from HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) policy checks then potentially upgraded from http:// to https://.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: The HSTS bypass name list should be empty in production environments. Adding hostnames bypasses strict transport security and re-enables downgrade attacks on those hosts. Only populate for specific internal hosts that cannot serve valid TLS and have no remediation path.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Configure the list of types that are excluded from synchronization
Description: This policy setting allows you to specify data types that will be limited/excluded from uploading data to the Microsoft Edge synchronization service.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling Microsoft sync prevents browser data (history, passwords, favourites) from leaving the managed device. Essential for data governance in M365-managed SMBs. Only deviate if cross-device sync is a documented business requirement.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Configure users ability to override feature flags
Description: This policy setting configures users' ability to override state of feature flags. Feature flags are settings a team can define that indicate whether a given set of features is visible in the user experience and/or invoked within the functionality.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Preventing users from overriding feature flags ensures Edge remains in its managed configuration state. Enabling user flag overrides can introduce untested features and bypass IT-configured settings.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Continue running background apps after Microsoft Edge closes
Description: This policy setting determines whether processes from Microsoft Edge may start at Operating System sign-in and continue running once an Edge browser window is closed. This allows background apps and the current browsing session to remain active, including any session cookies. An open background process displays an icon in the system tray and can always be closed from there.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Allowing apps to run after Edge closes keeps progressive web apps (PWAs) active. Low risk; disable if users report unexpected resource usage from background Edge processes.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Control communication with the Experimentation and Configuration Service
Description: This policy setting controls whether Microsoft Edge uses the Experimentation and Configuration Service to deploy the Experimentation and Configuration payload which consists of a list of early in development features that Microsoft is enabling for testing and feedback.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: 'control communication with the experimentation and configuration service' is a complex Edge policy with potential dependencies on other browser features or web apps. Engage with the client to map dependencies before enforcing. Use Edge policy reporting to validate impact before enforcement.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Control use of insecure content exceptions
Description: This policy setting allows for the configuration for users to add exceptions to allow mixed content for specific sites.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Preventing users from allowing insecure (mixed HTTP/HTTPS) content maintains TLS integrity on HTTPS pages. Only relax for internal sites that cannot be updated to full HTTPS — add per-site exceptions rather than a global allow.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - DNS interception checks enabled
Description: This policy setting determines whether a local switch is configured for DNS interception checks. These checks attempt to discover if the browser is behind a proxy that redirects unknown host names
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: DNS interception checks help detect captive portals and network interception. Low-risk to enable; only disable if a network appliance generates false positive interception detections.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Delete old browser data on migration
Description: This policy controls whether web browser data is deleted after migration to Microsoft Edge, this data includes forms, passwords, and visited sites.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Deleting old browser data during migration removes stale personal data from managed profiles. Low-risk; only skip if users need to retain legacy browser data during a phased migration.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Disable Bing chat entry-points on Microsoft Edge Enterprise new tab page
Description: By default, there are two Bing Chat entry-points on the new tab page. One is inside the new tab page search box, and one is in the Bing Autosuggest drawer on-click.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling Bing Chat / Copilot entry points in Edge prevents users from sharing page content with AI services without explicit consent. Apply in environments with data classification requirements; communicate the change to users.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Disable saving browser history
Description: This policy controls whether browser history is saved and prevents users from changing the policy.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Enforcing browsing data clearing on exit reduces residual data exposure on shared or unattended devices. Users on dedicated personal devices may find this disruptive; balance privacy requirements with usability.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Disable synchronization of data using Microsoft sync services
Description: This policy setting controls whether data synchronization with Microsoft sync services is allowed as well as whether the sync consent prompt appears to users. Examples of synced data include, but are not limited to, history and favorites
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling Microsoft sync prevents browser data (history, passwords, favourites) from leaving the managed device. Essential for data governance in M365-managed SMBs. Only deviate if cross-device sync is a documented business requirement.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Edge 3P SERP Telemetry Enabled
Description: This policy setting controls Edge3P Telemetry in Microsoft Edge. Edge3P Telemetry captures the searches a user does on third-party search providers without identifying the person or the device.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling Edge consumer engagement features (Follow, Sidebar, Guided Switch) reduces data telemetry and non-work distractions. No business functionality is impacted; these are consumer-oriented browser features.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Edge Wallet E-Tree Enabled
Description: This policy settings configures the use of the Wallet E-Tree feature in Microsoft Edge.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling Edge consumer features (Shopping, Rewards, Wallet, CryptoWallet) removes non-business browser functions. No business impact; reduces distraction and potential data sharing with Microsoft consumer services.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Enable AutoFill for addresses
Description: This policy controls whether the AutoFill feature of Microsoft Edge is enabled for the auto-complete feature for addresses and other information in web forms.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling address autofill prevents the browser from storing personal address data locally. Low operational impact; users can still manually enter addresses. Acceptable trade-off for data privacy.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Enable AutoFill for payment instructions
Description: This policy setting controls whether users can utilize payment information, such as credit or debit cards in web forms using previously stored information.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling payment autofill prevents the browser from storing payment card data, reducing credential/financial data exposure. Some users may find this inconvenient; communicate the change and note that password manager integrations are unaffected.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Enable CryptoWallet feature
Description: The CryptoWallet feature allows users to securely store, manage, and transact digital assets such as Bitcoin, Ethereum, and other cryptocurrencies
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling Edge consumer features (Shopping, Rewards, Wallet, CryptoWallet) removes non-business browser functions. No business impact; reduces distraction and potential data sharing with Microsoft consumer services.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Enable Discover access to page contents for AAD profiles
Description: This policy setting controls discover access to page contents for AAD profiles. Discover is an extension that hosts Bing Chat and in order to summarize pages and interact with text selections, it needs to be able to access the page contents. When enabled, page contents will be sent to Bing.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling Bing Chat / Copilot entry points in Edge prevents users from sharing page content with AI services without explicit consent. Apply in environments with data classification requirements; communicate the change to users.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Enable Follow service in Microsoft Edge
Description: This policy setting allows the Microsoft Edge browser to enable the follow service which allows users to follow an influencer, site, or topic in Microsoft Edge.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling Edge consumer engagement features (Follow, Sidebar, Guided Switch) reduces data telemetry and non-work distractions. No business functionality is impacted; these are consumer-oriented browser features.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Enable Google Cast
Description: This policy setting determines whether Google Cast is available to users
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling Google Cast removes the ability to cast browser content to Chromecast/Cast-capable devices. Only enable if users legitimately use Chromecast for presentations; low security risk either way.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Enable Microsoft Defender SmartScreen DNS requests
Description: This policy setting configures DNS requests made by Microsoft Defender SmartScreen
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Microsoft Defender SmartScreen is a key browser-level phishing and malware protection layer. Only skip if a third-party DNS filter or web proxy already provides equivalent real-time URL reputation checking.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Enable browser legacy extension point blocking
Description: This policy setting sets the ProcessExtensionPointDisablePolicy on Microsoft Edge´s browser process to block code injection from legacy third party applications.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Blocking legacy browser extension injection points prevents DLL-injection attacks via older browser hooks. Only disable if a specific LOB tool explicitly requires legacy extension point access — contact the vendor for a modern alternative.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Enable component updates in Microsoft Edge
Description: This policy determines whether updates for Microsoft Edge components are enabled in Microsoft Edge.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Edge update policies should align with the organisation's patch management cadence. Ensure updates are not blocked for extended periods; use Intune Update Rings or equivalent to manage timing.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Enable deleting browser and download history
Description: This policy controls whether users can delete browser and download history for Microsoft Edge.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: 'enable deleting browser and download history' has moderate implementation risk. Validate against existing browser workflows and extensions; pilot on a test group before broad rollout.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Enable globally scoped HTTP auth cache
Description: This policy setting controls whether HTTP auth credentials may be automatically used in the context of another web site visited in Microsoft Edge.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling globally scoped HTTP auth cache prevents authentication credentials for one site from being reused by other pages. Reduces credential reuse risk with minimal impact on modern web apps that use token-based auth.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Enable profile creation from the Identity flyout menu or the Settings page
Description: This policy setting controls whether user profiles can create new profiles in Microsoft Edge.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Blocking self-service profile creation prevents users from adding personal Microsoft accounts to the managed Edge browser. Maintain corporate profile integrity; only enable if a specific multi-identity workflow is approved.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Enable resolution of navigation errors using a web service
Description: This policy setting controls whether Microsoft Edge can issue a dataless connection to a web service to probe networks, (ex: Hotel and Airport Wi-Fi) for connectivity issues.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling the web service for navigation error resolution prevents page-not-found queries being sent to Google/Microsoft. Privacy control; negligible UX impact since the feature primarily provides suggestions for mistyped URLs.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Enable saving passwords to the password manager
Description: This policy setting enables or disables the ability for users to save their passwords in Microsoft Edge.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling the built-in password manager forces users to a centrally managed password manager (e.g., 1Password, Bitwarden). Communicate the policy change and ensure an approved alternative is deployed before enforcing.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Enable security warnings for command-line flags
Description: This policy setting prevents Microsoft Edge from showing security warnings that potentially dangerous command-line flags are in use at its' launch.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Suppressing security warnings for unsafe command-line flags makes it easier to exploit Edge via custom flags. No valid operational reason to disable this in a managed SMB environment.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Enable site isolation for every site
Description: This policy setting ensures that each website runs in its own process so that a site will not be able to utilize or take data from another running site.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Site isolation is a defence-in-depth control against cross-site data leakage attacks (Spectre/Meltdown mitigations). Memory overhead is the only trade-off; only disable on severely RAM-constrained devices.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Enable startup boost
Description: This policy setting allows Microsoft Edge processes to start at OS sign-in and restart in background after the last browser window is closed. If Microsoft Edge is running in background mode, the browser might not close when the last window is closed, and the browser won´t be restarted in background when the window closes. See the BackgroundModeEnabled (Continue running background apps after Microsoft Edge closes) policy for information about what happens after configuring Microsoft Edge background mode behavior.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Startup boost keeps Edge processes running in the background after closing, reducing load time. Security-neutral; only disable if background processes are a concern on low-spec devices.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Enable tab organization suggestions
Description: This policy setting controls whether Microsoft Edge can use its tab organization service to help name or suggest tab groups.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling AI-powered tab organization suggestions prevents page content from being sent to Microsoft AI services. Privacy control; no business functionality is lost — users can still organise tabs manually.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Enable the Search bar
Description: This policy setting configures the use of the search bar. The search bar is used to search the web from a user's desktop or from an application. The search bar provides a search box, powered by Edge default search engine, that shows web suggestions and opens all web searches in Microsoft Edge.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling the Edge sidebar search bar reduces unnecessary UI surface and avoids ambient data collection. Low operational impact; users can still search via the address bar.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Enable the linked account feature
Description: This policy setting determines if Microsoft Edge can guide a user to the account management page where they can link a Microsoft Account (MSA) to an Azure Active Directory (Entra ID) account.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling the linked account feature prevents personal Microsoft account linking in the work Edge profile. Keeps corporate and personal identities separate; no business justification to enable in a managed SMB.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Enable upload files from mobile in Microsoft Edge desktop
Description: This policy settings allows the configuration of the Edge "Upload from mobile" feature. The "Upload from mobile" feature allows users to select file(s) from a mobile device and upload to a via a webpage in Microsoft Edge
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling mobile file upload integration removes a consumer cross-device feature rarely needed in managed SMBs. Low operational impact; enterprise file sharing should use approved cloud storage (SharePoint, OneDrive).

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Enable use of ephemeral profiles
Description: This policy setting controls whether user profiles are switched to ephemeral mode. In ephemeral mode, profile data is saved on disk for the length of the session and then the data is deleted after the session is over. Therefore, no data is saved to the device.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Ephemeral profiles wipe all browser data on close, which can conflict with Intune-managed settings persistence. Use only for kiosk/shared-device scenarios; avoid on standard user endpoints.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Enable warnings for insecure forms
Description: This policy setting controls the handling of insecure forms (forms submitted over HTTP) embedded in secure (HTTPS) sites in the browser. When enabled, a full-page warning will be shown, and autofill will be disabled for those forms. When disabled, warnings will not be shown for insecure forms, and autofill will work normally.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Showing warnings for forms submitted over HTTP is a low-friction security signal. Only disable if internal legacy forms generate false-positive warnings and cannot be migrated to HTTPS.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Enables DALL-E themes generation
Description: This policy setting configures the use of generated browser themes using DALL-E and apply them to Microsoft Edge. DALL-E is an open Artificial Intelligence (AI) system that creates realistic images and art from text descriptions (prompts).
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling Edge AI writing and image generation features prevents page content from being submitted to Microsoft AI services. Appropriate for environments with data handling obligations; no core productivity feature is lost.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Guided Switch Enabled
Description: This policy setting allows Microsoft Edge to prompt the user to switch to the appropriate profile when Microsoft Edge detects that a link is a personal or work link.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling Edge consumer engagement features (Follow, Sidebar, Guided Switch) reduces data telemetry and non-work distractions. No business functionality is impacted; these are consumer-oriented browser features.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Hide the First-run experience and splash screen
Description: This policy setting controls whether the First-run experience and splash screen is presented to the user the first time Microsoft Edge is opened. Some of the options presented to the user include the ability to import data from other web browsers on the system.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Hiding the Edge first-run splash screen reduces user prompts to add personal accounts or import personal data. Recommended for managed deployments; no functionality is lost.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - In-app support Enabled
Description: This policy setting allows users to contact in-app Microsoft support agents directly from the Microsoft Edge browser.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling built-in feedback and support channels prevents telemetry and user data from being sent to Microsoft/Google via these paths. IT support should provide an alternative channel; users may initially miss the quick feedback button.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Manage exposure of local IP addresses by WebRTC
Description: This policy setting specifies a list of URLs or patterns which local IP address will be exposed by WebRTC.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Managing WebRTC local IP address exposure prevents internal network topology leakage through browser-based video calls. The recommended DisableNonProxiedUdp or HideMyLocalIp setting reduces risk with minimal Teams/Zoom impact.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Prevent bypassing Microsoft Defender SmartScreen prompts for sites
Description: This policy setting controls whether users may bypass the SmartScreen warning if a site is deemed unsafe.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Microsoft Defender SmartScreen is a key browser-level phishing and malware protection layer. Only skip if a third-party DNS filter or web proxy already provides equivalent real-time URL reputation checking.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Set disk cache size, in bytes
Description: This setting controls the size of the cache, in bytes, used to store files on the disk.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Setting a maximum disk cache size limits Edge disk usage on constrained devices. The CIS recommended value (250 MB) is a reasonable cap; adjust upward for power users with high web app usage.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Set the time period for update notifications
Description: This setting does not determine if updates are applied, the policy setting allows setting a time period in which users are notified that Microsoft Edge has been updated and must be closed and re-opened.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Edge update policies should align with the organisation's patch management cadence. Ensure updates are not blocked for extended periods; use Intune Update Rings or equivalent to manage timing.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Shopping in Microsoft Edge Enabled
Description: This policy setting allows users to compare the prices of products, get coupons or rebates from the website, auto-apply coupons, and help checkout faster using autofill data. Coupons for the current retailer and prices from other retailers will be fetched from a server.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling Edge consumer features (Shopping, Rewards, Wallet, CryptoWallet) removes non-business browser functions. No business impact; reduces distraction and potential data sharing with Microsoft consumer services.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Show Microsoft Rewards experiences
Description: This policy setting controls whether the Microsoft Reward experience is available to users and if notifications are received. The Microsoft Rewards experience is a free program that allows the user to earn points when searching on Bing.com. With these points, the users can buy merchandise from the Microsoft Store online and in Windows 10.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling Edge consumer features (Shopping, Rewards, Wallet, CryptoWallet) removes non-business browser functions. No business impact; reduces distraction and potential data sharing with Microsoft consumer services.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Show the Reload in Internet Explorer mode button in the toolbar
Description: This policy setting shows the Reload in Internet Explorer mode button in the toolbar. IE Mode in Microsoft Edge allows organizations that still need Internet Explorer 11, (which is not supported) for backward compatibility with existing websites.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Hiding the IE mode reload button discourages reliance on legacy IE rendering. Only enable if specific internal web apps require IE mode and are awaiting modernisation.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Standalone Sidebar Enabled
Description: This policy setting controls whether users will have the ability to activate the standalone sidebar. The standalone sidebar is an optional mode for the sidebar in Microsoft Edge and uses Bing AI. When this mode is activated by a user, the sidebar appears in a fixed position on the Microsoft Windows desktop and is hidden from the browser application frame.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling Edge consumer engagement features (Follow, Sidebar, Guided Switch) reduces data telemetry and non-work distractions. No business functionality is impacted; these are consumer-oriented browser features.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Suggest similar pages when a webpage can’t be found
Description: This policy setting controls whether Microsoft Edge may connect to a web service to generate URLs and search suggestions for website connectivity issues. If disabled standard errors will be issued, if enabled errors will be customized with URL suggestions.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: 'suggest similar pages when a webpage can’t be found' is a low-complexity, single-value setting with minimal operational impact. Apply the recommended state; deviation requires a specific documented business or technical exception.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Suppress the unsupported OS warning
Description: This policy setting suppresses the warning that appears when Microsoft Edge is running on a computer or operating system that is no longer supported. If this policy is disabled or unset, the warnings will appear on such unsupported computers or operating systems.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Suppressing the unsupported OS warning hides a security signal — it should be shown. The recommended setting is Disabled (do not suppress warnings). Only deviate if OS upgrade cannot be expedited and the warning causes user confusion.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Update policy override default
Description: This policy settings sets the default behavior for all channels concerning the way Microsoft Edge Update handles available updates for Microsoft Edge.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Edge update policies should align with the organisation's patch management cadence. Ensure updates are not blocked for extended periods; use Intune Update Rings or equivalent to manage timing.

Name: CISv3 - EDGE - L1 - Wallet Donation Enabled
Description: The Wallet Donation feature in Microsoft Edge allows users to view their donation summary, explore Nonprofit organizations (NPOs), donate to an NPO, manage their monthly donations, and view their donation history.
SMB Justification (if not using recommen: Disabling Edge consumer features (Shopping, Rewards, Wallet, CryptoWallet) removes non-business browser functions. No business impact; reduces distraction and potential data sharing with Microsoft consumer services.
